Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
359 AM EDT Wed Sep 23 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
A Small Craft Advisory was issued for all waters Thursday into
Thursday night. Coastal Flood headlines were also extended
further out in time.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Cloudy, showery, and cool conditions continue through much
  of the day today, with drier conditions building back in for 
  Thursday and Friday.

- 2) Breezy and warmer this weekend, but forecast remains uncertain
  as Nor'easter impacts Northeast U.S.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1... Cloudy, showery, and cool conditions continue 
through much of the day today, with drier conditions building 
back in for Thursday and Friday.

As of 330 AM, radar imagery shows steady rain in place for most
locations east of the Blue Ridge/south of I-70. Conditions have
largely dried out to the west of the Blue Ridge, other than some
spotty drizzle. To the north of I-70/east of the Blue Ridge the
precipitation shield is a bit more broken up/showery in nature.

A strong cold-air damming (CAD) wedge remains in place across 
the entire area along with the aforementioned rain, cloudy 
skies, and cool temperatures. An unseasonably strong area of 
high pressure centered to our north across southern Quebec will 
reach peak strength today. As this occurs, drier air will slowly
start to filter into the area from the northeast. This drier 
air will slowly start to break down the precipitation shield, 
with rain gradually coming to an end from northeast to 
southwest over the course of the day. Locations in central 
Virginia will be the last to see the precipitation/low clouds 
break up later tonight. Even after the precipitation comes to 
an end, it will still be a cool day with cloudy skies in place. 
Temperatures are only forecast to make it into the 50s to near 
60 to the west of the Blue Ridge, and then low to mid 60s to the
east of the Blue Ridge. Winds will remain gusty out of the 
northeast, with gusts to around 20-30 mph possible at times to 
the east of the Blue Ridge.

Drier conditions are forecast for Thursday and Friday as the 
upper trough axis that has been stalled out to our west finally 
starts to make some eastward progress. This trough axis will 
pass overhead tomorrow, and then progress offshore on Friday. As
this occurs, a coastal low will deepen off to our east in 
response. The pressure gradient between the high to our north 
and the developing coastal low will keep winds gusty out of the 
north to northeast. Temperatures will stay below normal as a 
result, with highs in the 60s tomorrow, and then upper 60s to 
near 70 on Friday.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Breezy and warmer this weekend, but forecast remains 
uncertain as Nor'easter impacts Northeast U.S. 

Anomalously strong surface ridge (by late September standards) 
begins to weaken this weekend as a strong Nor'easter develops off 
the coast of Southern New England/LI. Ensemble members still show 
quite a bit of spread regarding the exact track of the Nor'easter. A 
few members show the possibility the low tracks closer to the NJ / 
Delmarva coast this weekend. Regardless of exact position, we are 
likely to be on the drier side of the system with northwest winds 
bringing in breezy, warmer, and mostly dry conditions. If the 
Nor'easter tracks closer to our area that could bring some rain 
chances to the area, especially along/east of I-95, along with the 
potential for increasing winds. Safe to say that there isn't a 
definite trend for this weekend, so be sure to keep track of the 
forecast for any changes in the coming days.

The Nor'easter is eventually pushed offshore at the start of next 
week as high pressure builds in from the OH Valley and Great Lakes. 
Mid-level ridging builds over much of the eastern CONUS during the 
middle of next week, marking the return of much warmer temperatures 
and continued dry conditions. 

&&

.AVIATION /07Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
As of 330 AM, many locations have actually improved back to 
MVFR/VFR, with only CHO observing IFR at the moment. Any 
locations that have improved back to VFR are expected to drop 
back to MVFR after sunrise. Thereafter, dry air is expected to 
make very slow southwestward progress throughout the day. 
Showers likely come to an end at most terminals mid- late 
morning or early afternoon. VFR ceilings are expected to reach 
the DC Metro terminals by late afternoon. Winds today will be 
gusty out of the northeast. VFR conditions are expected for all 
on Thursday and Friday, along with gusty north to northeasterly 
winds. 

A strong Nor'easter off the coast near Southern New England to NJ 
will bring breezy northwest winds this weekend (gusts around 20-25 
knots possible). Some showers are possible, but highly uncertain as 
it will depend how close the low pressure gets to our area. Continue 
to monitor for any additional impacts.

&&

.MARINE...
Winds will remain gusty out of the northeast over the waters for
the foreseeable future. Gale Warnings go into effect for the
waters surrounding Southern Maryland this morning, with high end
SCAs (gusts to near 30 kt) in effect elsewhere. Small Craft
Advisories have been issued for all waters Thursday through
Thursday night, for continued gusty northeasterly winds. SCAs
will likely be needed again in northerly flow on Friday.

High-end SCA conditions to Gales are possible this weekend over the 
waters, especially in the Chesapeake Bay due to the strong 
Nor'easter that will be off the coast. If the low tracks closer to 
our area, expect higher gusts over the waters. However, there 
remains a lot of uncertainty in the forecast, so be sure to check 
back as conditions become more certain through the week.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
A long duration coastal flood event is expected over the next
several days within persistent onshore flow. Changes to
headlines were relatively small overnight, with the various
headlines just being pushed a bit further out in time. Coastal
Flood Advisories for Annapolis and Straits Point through tonight
are followed by Coastal Flood Watches tomorrow through Friday
morning. At Alexandria, a Coastal Flood Advisory today through
tomorrow morning is followed with a Coastal Flood Watch tomorrow
afternoon through Friday morning. At Dahlgren and Solomons
Island, Coastal Flood Advisories extend through Thursday night.
Anomalies will be lower further north on the Bay, but we'll need
to keep an eye on Baltimore and Havre de Grace later in the
week, as well as DC on the Upper Tidal Potomac. Decisions will
likely need to be made this morning regarding whether Watches
are converted to Warnings or Advisories.

&&

.LWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...

MD...Small Craft Advisory until 6 AM EDT Friday for MDZ008.
     Coastal Flood Advisory until midnight EDT tonight for MDZ014.
     Coastal Flood Watch from late tonight through Friday morning

     Coastal Flood Advisory until 8 PM EDT this evening for MDZ017.
     Coastal Flood Watch from this evening through Friday afternoon

     Coastal Flood Advisory until 8 AM EDT Friday for MDZ018.
VA...Coastal Flood Advisory until 7 AM EDT Friday for VAZ057.
     Coastal Flood Advisory until 2 PM EDT Thursday for VAZ054.
     Coastal Flood Watch from Thursday afternoon through Friday 
     morning for VAZ054.

     536-538>540.
     Small Craft Advisory until 6 AM EDT early this morning for 
     ANZ533-534-537-541>543.
     Small Craft Advisory from 6 AM Thursday to 6 AM EDT Friday for 
     ANZ533-534-537-541>543.
     Gale Warning until 6 AM EDT Thursday for ANZ533-534-537-
     541>543.

&&
